title: Gram scale preparation of clozapine N-oxide (CNO), a synthetic small molecule actuator for muscarinic acetylcholine DREADDs
author: van der Peet, Gunawan, et al.

steps.title: Extract clozapine from tablets
steps.instruction: Crush tablets, extract with acetone, filter, concentrate, precipitate with petroleum spirit, collect crystals, and record analytical data.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 100 Clopine tablets (Pfizer, each 100 mg clozapine) and crush them to a fine powder.
Add the powder to 250 mL acetone in a suitable flask and stir at 50 °C for 60 min.
Filter the hot mixture through a pad of Celite, rinsing the pad with additional acetone.
Reduce the volume of the filtrate under vacuum to obtain a concentrated residue.
Add petroleum spirit dropwise to the concentrate until crystals first appear.
Cool the suspension on ice, then filter to collect the yellow crystals (9.8 g, 98% yield).
Record the melting point (183–184 °C) and compare with literature (182–184 °C).
Obtain HRMS (ESI) m/z: calculated for C₁₈H₂₀ClN₄ [M+H]⁺ 327.1371, found 327.1372.

steps.title: Oxidize clozapine to N‑oxide
steps.instruction: React clozapine with Oxone under basic conditions, purify by chromatography, crystallize, and record analytical data.

substeps.instruction: Weigh Oxone® monopersulfate (4.29 g, 6.68 mmol).
In a reaction flask, dissolve clozapine (4.37 g, 13.4 mmol) and NaHCO₃ (2.25 g, 26.7 mmol) in 25 mL methanol and 5 mL water at room temperature.
Add the Oxone portionwise to the stirred solution at r.t. and continue stirring for 2 h at r.t.
Concentrate the reaction mixture under reduced pressure.
Purify the crude material by silica‑gel column chromatography using 60 % CH₂Cl₂/MeOH as eluent to afford an orange oil.
Crystallize the oil from ethanol (EtOH) to obtain clozapine‑N‑oxide as the EtOH solvate (4.46 g, 97% yield).
Record the melting point (235–237 °C) and compare with literature values (224 °C from EtOH; 248–249 °C from EtOAc; 199–206 °C).
Obtain HRMS (ESI) m/z: calculated for C₁₈H₂₀ClN₄O [M+H]⁺ 343.1320, found 343.1322.

steps.title: Maintain CHO‑FlpIn cells
steps.instruction: Culture CHO‑FlpIn cells expressing human M1 DREADD in DMEM with supplements at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

substeps.instruction: Grow the cells in Dulbecco’s Modified Eagle Medium (DMEM) supplemented with 10 % fetal bovine serum (FBS) and 0.6 mg mL⁻¹ hygromycin B.
Incubate at 37 °C in a humidified incubator with 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Immunostain brain sections
steps.instruction: Perfuse rats, fix and cryoprotect brains, section, block, incubate with primary and secondary antibodies, wash, mount, and image.

substeps.instruction: Deeply anaesthetize rats with pentobarbitone (100 mg kg⁻¹, i.p.).
Transcardially perfuse each rat with 300 mL ice‑cold 0.1 M phosphate‑buffered saline (PBS) followed by 400 mL 4 % formaldehyde in PBS.
Dissect the brains and submerge them in 30 % sucrose in PBS for 48 h at 4 °C.
Cut coronal sections (30 µm) through the brainstem (NI region) and collect free‑floating sections in PBS.
Incubate sections in blocking buffer (10 % v/v normal goat serum (NGS) in PBS with 0.1 % Triton‑X) for 1 h with agitation at room temperature.
Incubate sections in PBS containing mouse anti‑relaxin‑3 (1 : 5, catalog HK4‑144‑10; 2 % NGS, 0.1 % Triton‑X) for 18 h at room temperature.
Wash sections 3 × 10 min with PBS.
Incubate sections in PBS with Alexa Fluor‑488‑conjugated donkey anti‑mouse (1 : 500 dilution; Jackson ImmunoResearch) for 1 h at room temperature.
Wash sections 3 × 5 min with PBS.
Mount sections on slides, coverslip with Fluoromount‑G (Southern Biotech).
Acquire stitched image tiles using a Zeiss LSM 780 confocal microscope as described in reference [12].
